headline: Anxiety is suffering about imagined futures—worry that anticipates pain that may never come
universal_truth: You can only experience the present; anxiety trades real now for imagined later; most worries never happen
fun_facts: Studies show 85% of things people worry about never actually happen
Of the 15% that do happen, 79% of people say they handled it better than expected
Chronic worry doesn't prepare you—it depletes resources without providing benefit
discussion_questions: How much of your suffering is about imagined futures versus present reality?
What percentage of your past worries actually came true?
How do you distinguish useful anticipation from harmful anxiety?

hook.script: Right now, you're probably fine. But in your mind, you might be suffering about tomorrow, next week, next year. Anxiety is experiencing pain that hasn't happened yet—and mostly never will. Most worries are tickets to suffering you never have to pay.

cliff.script: Worry feels like preparation. But is it actually helping? What's the difference between useful anticipation and harmful anxiety?
cliff.prompt: When does worry help versus hurt?

options.text: Useful anticipation leads to action—you identify a problem and address it; anxiety just circles endlessly without solving anything, depleting resources for suffering that likely won't happen
options.response: Yes. The test: Does this worry lead to action? If you can do something, do it and stop worrying. If you can't do anything, worrying is just prepaying pain you may never owe.
Natural doesn't mean helpful—worry evolved for different circumstances than we face...

fact1.title: The False Tax
fact1.script: Worry is paying a tax on trouble that may never arrive. Studies show most worries don't happen. You're experiencing suffering for nothing—suffering real, trouble imaginary.

fact2.title: Action or Accept
fact2.script: Useful worry leads to action. If you can do something, do it. If you can't, accept and redirect attention. Spinning in worry without action is the worst option.

fact3.title: Present Moment
fact3.script: You can only experience now. Anxiety pulls you into an imagined future. Return to the present—usually, right now, you're okay. The suffering is in your head, not in reality.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: You can only experience the present. Anxiety trades real now for imagined later. Most worries never happen. Return to now.

outro.script: That's Day 318. Tomorrow, we'll explore stopping hurt before it starts—prevention. Until then, notice how much of your suffering is about imagined futures.

growTrack.title: Worry Audit - What Are You Pre-Suffering?
growTrack.learning_objective: Distinguish useful anticipation from harmful anxiety
growTrack.activity: List your current worries. For each: Is this likely to happen? Can I do something about it? If yes, do it. If no, practice letting it go. How much of your suffering is about imagined futures?
